ut.title: Ultrasonic Thickness Testing & UT Inspection | Baltimore, MD
ut.description: Ultrasonic thickness testing and UT weld inspection on harbor steel, tanks, vessels and piping in Baltimore, MD. ASNT Level II technicians. Get a quote.
ut.h1: Ultrasonic Testing (UT) Inspection in Baltimore, Maryland
ut.html:
Baltimore sits on salt water, and salt water eats steel. Atlantis NDT mobilizes Level II technicians to Baltimore terminals, yards, plants and structures for ultrasonic thickness testing and ultrasonic weld examination: wall loss on tanks, vessels and piping, plate thickness on pier and vessel steel, and weld quality in groove joints. Send the component, the code and the site to a quote request and we reply within one business day.

Where ultrasonic testing is used around the Port of Baltimore

The Port of Baltimore handles containers, autos, roll-on roll-off cargo, bulk and liquids across a string of terminals on the Patapsco River. Each terminal is a stock of welded and bolted steel exposed to spray and tidal wetting: pier decks and bulkheads, crane rails and crane structures, fuel and chemical storage tanks, loading piping and the pressure equipment of terminal utilities. Ship repair yards add hull plate, tanks and piping on vessels, where owners want thickness readings for their own repair planning.

Sparrows Point is the largest change on the map. The former Bethlehem Steel mill is being redeveloped, and a new container terminal on 168 acres broke ground in May 2026 with deep-water berths and large cranes planned. Heavy new steel construction and the older plant still standing there both need thickness and weld examination. Elsewhere in the metropolitan area, power and steam plants, hospital campuses, sugar and food processing, chemical blending and the region's bridges all rely on steel that corrodes, erodes or fatigues, and thickness readings are the most direct way to follow that damage.

What ultrasonic testing finds and what it misses

An ultrasonic instrument launches a sound pulse into the metal and measures the time for the echo. For thickness, the time converts straight into remaining wall. For welds, echoes from inside the volume show lack of fusion, slag and cracks. The method also locates laminations in plate and some forging flaws.

In a harbor setting, the limits are mostly about condition. Marine coatings can be thick and layered, and sound passes through a well-bonded coating but not through a blistered or disbonded one. Pitting from chloride attack makes the back wall irregular, so a reading may jump around from point to point, and a single number can understate the worst local loss. Heavy scale, mussel and barnacle growth or marine fouling must be cleaned from the test spot. Corrosion that runs along a seam or a groove may miss a grid point, which is why the reading pattern matters. Surface-breaking cracks on weld toes are often confirmed with magnetic particle inspection in Baltimore or liquid penetrant testing in Baltimore.

Codes and the Maryland regime for Baltimore equipment

Weld examination follows ASME Section V Article 4 with acceptance taken from the construction code: ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 12 for vessels, ASME B31.3 Table 341.3.2 for process piping, ASME B31.1 for power piping, or AWS D1.1 for structural steel. Thickness work follows ASME Section V Article 23 (SE-797) and ASTM E797. For in-service tanks, vessels and piping, API 653, API 510 and API 570 apply, and the owner's authorized inspector is the inspector of record. Atlantis performs the examination and delivers the data, including thickness at condition monitoring locations.

Maryland has its own boiler and pressure vessel regime. The Maryland Division of Labor and Industry runs a Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Program under the state's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act. Inspections are carried out by inspectors commissioned by the National Board and the state who work for an authorized inspection agency, equipment must be built to the ASME Code and registered with the National Board, and a valid certificate of inspection is required to operate a boiler. Whether a given vessel is covered, and on what interval, is a question for the owner's inspection agency. Plants under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 use ultrasonic data in their mechanical integrity records, and our guide to Article 5 thickness requirements explains the technical background.

Thickness surveys on coastal and marine steel

Dual-element probes are the first choice on corroded surfaces because the separate transmit and receive crystals cope better with pitting than a single crystal does. The technician calibrates on a step block of the same steel, rechecks calibration during the job, and watches the A-scan so that a double echo on thin plate or a lamination echo is not mistaken for the true back wall. A bare digital readout cannot show that.

On tanks, readings are taken on shell courses, the annular plate region and, where accessible, the bottom plate. On piping, a grid at elbows, tees, reducers and low points follows the places erosion and condensate attack concentrate. Hot lines need a high-temperature probe, couplant and a temperature correction. Insulated or coated lines need the covering removed at the points to be read, and the owner arranges that. We mark every location on a sketch so the next survey reads the same spots and the trend is meaningful. For vessel plate, readings support the owner's repair estimate and condition decisions. Readings meant for credit to a classification society survey must come from a firm that society has approved, so ask your surveyor what is acceptable before the job. See our national ultrasonic testing page for the overall service.

Barges, hull plate and steel repair planning

Vessel work has a different rhythm from plant work. A barge, tug or work boat in a repair yard has plate whose condition decides how much steel is cropped and renewed, and thickness readings taken before the work starts let the owner estimate quantities and negotiate the repair specification with facts in hand. Readings are laid out by frame and strake, tied to a sketch, and compared with the original plan thickness where drawings exist. Tanks, void spaces and ballast compartments need confined-space entry arrangements, ventilation and a standby person, all of which the yard or owner provides. Coatings inside tanks are often hard and thick, so decide in advance where they will be removed for gauging.

Documentation and traceability on thickness work

Thickness data is only useful if the next survey can repeat it. Each point carries a reference number that matches the sketch, the probe and gauge are named, and the calibration block is identified, so a later technician can return to the same spot with the same method and see real change. Owners who trend corrosion across several campaigns usually ask for the data in a spreadsheet as well as the signed report, and that is easy to arrange when it is requested up front.

Ultrasonic weld examination with angle beams

Groove welds are scanned with shear-wave angle beams, commonly 45, 60 or 70 degrees, from both sides when access permits. A reference level or distance-amplitude curve is built from side-drilled holes in a block of similar material, the full weld and heat-affected zone are covered, and each indication is judged on amplitude, length and position against the code table. Lack of fusion along the bevel face and slag lines are the typical findings.

Bridge, crane and fabrication steel often calls for AWS D1.1 or D1.5 criteria, which have their own ultrasonic acceptance tables, so name the code when you ask for a quote. Weld geometry decides what is possible. Branch connections, node joints and small-bore pipe may not allow a full scan, and the report records any coverage limitation instead of hiding it. Replacing film or image work with ultrasonic examination is a code decision that the owner, engineer and authorized inspector have to make before work starts.

Who does the work

Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, reviews the Level III side of our work. Technicians who set up, calibrate and interpret are Level II under Atlantis's written practice, which is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and a Level III approves procedures and reviews reports. Atlantis has no office in Baltimore, so technicians travel to your site for the agreed scope. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001.

What the ultrasonic report contains

Each report is written so the authorized inspector or engineer can use it without a phone call. It covers these points:

  • The component or line number, drawing reference, material, nominal thickness and minimum required thickness.
  • The procedure number and revision, plus the code and edition it follows.
  • The instrument, probes, wedges, couplant, calibration block and calibration checks.
  • The technician and level, and the Level III reviewer.
  • A thickness grid tied to a sketch, or weld indications with position, length and amplitude.
  • Accept or reject against the named criteria, and every limitation on coverage.

Where a reading approaches the minimum, the report shows nominal wall, measured wall and calculated loss side by side so the trend is plain. Locations that could not be read, such as a plate covered by a bolted fitting or a line under insulation that stayed in place, are listed with the reason so nobody assumes they were checked.

Planning an ultrasonic job in Baltimore

Baltimore summers are hot and humid and winters are cold and damp, and harbor spray and fog keep steel wet more often than inland. Wet steel must be dried before a weld scan, hot steel needs high-temperature materials, and cold weather stiffens couplant. Tell us the season of the work and whether the steel is exposed.

Access matters as much as weather. Many terminal areas are secure facilities, and workers there usually need a Transportation Worker Identification Credential, a site safety orientation and an escort. Plan for scaffolding or lift access to tank shells, crane structures and pier undersides, and for insulation and coating removal at the test points. Give us the location relative to I-95, I-695 and the harbor tunnels so travel is planned, and expect dates to be confirmed when the scope is agreed instead of at first contact.

Choosing between ultrasonic, magnetic particle and penetrant testing

Ultrasonic testing answers questions about wall and weld volume. Magnetic particle testing finds surface cracks in carbon steel quickly, and penetrant testing does the same on stainless steel, aluminum and nickel alloys. Many waterfront jobs use ultrasonic and magnetic particle testing together on the same weld. The ultrasonic testing guide explains the method in more depth.

Training your own ultrasonic technicians in Baltimore

Companies that would rather build in-house capability can use UT Level 1 training and UT Level 2 training, with simulator practice on the ultrasonic testing simulator. The employer provides hands-on practice and the practical exam and certifies its own people under its written practice. Start from the Baltimore NDT training page.

faq.q: Does Atlantis have an office or crew in Baltimore?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Baltimore. Technicians are mobilized to your terminal, yard or plant for the agreed scope, and dates are confirmed once the scope is defined and access has been arranged.

faq.q: Can ultrasonic readings be taken through marine paint?
faq.a: Sometimes. A well-bonded coating of limited thickness can be read through with the right probe and procedure, but blistered or disbonded coating blocks sound, so the technician may ask for coating removal at test points.

faq.q: Are your thickness readings acceptable for a classification society survey?
faq.a: Readings used for class credit must come from a firm approved by that vessel's society. Ask your surveyor first. Readings for an owner's own repair planning and condition decisions do not carry that requirement.

faq.q: What does ultrasonic testing show on tanks and piping at a terminal?
faq.a: It shows remaining wall at marked locations and can reveal laminations and weld flaws. Your authorized inspector uses the data under API 653, API 510 or API 570 to judge remaining life and the next interval.

faq.q: Which Maryland rules cover boilers and pressure vessels?
faq.a: The Maryland Division of Labor and Industry administers a Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Program. Covered equipment is inspected by commissioned inspectors from an authorized inspection agency, so confirm coverage and intervals with your agency.

faq.q: Do workers need special credentials at Baltimore marine terminals?
faq.a: Many secure terminal areas require a Transportation Worker Identification Credential, safety orientation and an escort. Tell us early which areas the job covers so the technician can arrange access before arrival.

faq.q: How should the surface be prepared for a thickness survey?
faq.a: Remove loose scale, marine growth, flaking paint and insulation at each test point, and leave bare steel or firmly bonded coating. Heavy corrosion products reduce signal quality and may need grinding before readings are reliable.

faq.q: Can ultrasonic testing replace radiography on a weld?
faq.a: Only when the governing code permits it and the owner, engineer and authorized inspector agree before the job. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States, so volumetric work is done with ultrasonic methods where allowed.

faq.q: Can my team learn ultrasonic testing instead of hiring a crew?
faq.a: Yes. UT Level 1 and Level 2 courses are available, with practice on a simulator. Companies run the hands-on part and the practical exam themselves, then certify their own technicians under the written practice.

mt.title: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MT) in Baltimore, MD | MPI
mt.description: Magnetic particle testing for welds, cranes, pier steel and castings in Baltimore, MD. Yoke, prod and wet fluorescent methods by ASNT Level II. Get a quote.
mt.h1: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MT) in Baltimore, Maryland
mt.html:
Atlantis NDT mobilizes Level II technicians to Baltimore for magnetic particle inspection of carbon and low-alloy steel: crane structures at the harbor, weldments at fabrication shops and ship repair yards, bridge and pier steel, lifting gear and pressure equipment welds. We select the yoke, prod or wet fluorescent technique to suit the part and report every indication against the code you name. Use a quote request to send the scope and we reply within one business day.

Where magnetic particle testing is used in Baltimore

The harbor is the obvious starting point. Container and bulk terminals run large cranes whose booms, legs, trolley frames and machinery bases carry heavy cyclic loads, and the welds at stiffeners and brackets are fatigue-prone. Ship repair yards cut out and replace steel plate, weld on pads and brackets and rebuild machinery foundations, and every one of those repair welds is a candidate for surface crack examination.

Away from the water, Baltimore fabricators build structural steel, platforms, tanks and skids, and metal-working shops make forged and cast parts. Rail yards and trucking operations maintain frames, couplers and lifting equipment. Bridges are a constant presence in this city: the replacement of the Francis Scott Key Bridge after the March 2024 collapse is one of the largest steel projects on the East Coast, and the regional highway and rail network is full of welded girders where toe cracks develop. The redevelopment of the former Sparrows Point steel mill adds new terminal steel and the legacy plant equipment that comes with it.

What the method finds and where it stops

Magnetizing a steel part creates a field. If a crack breaks the surface or lies just beneath it, the field leaks out and holds fine iron particles in a visible line. Toe cracks, lack of fusion at the surface, laps, seams and fatigue cracks all show well, and the method is fast over large areas of weld.

The limits are firm. Only ferromagnetic material responds: carbon steel and most low-alloy steel. Austenitic stainless steel, aluminum and copper alloys do not, and parts made of them need penetrant testing. A flaw buried deeper than a few millimeters is invisible to the method, so it says nothing about weld volume or remaining wall. A crack parallel to the field is missed, which is why two directions are examined. Thick marine paint and heavy scale keep particles away from the steel. For the interior of a weld or the thickness of a plate, ultrasonic testing in Baltimore is the right tool.

Codes and acceptance criteria for waterfront steel

Procedures follow ASME Section V Article 7 and ASTM E1444, with ASTM E709 as the guide to the method. Acceptance criteria come from the governing code: ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 6 for pressure vessels, ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.3 and Table 341.3.2 for process piping, AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for highway bridge steel. For in-service tanks, vessels and piping under API 653, API 510 and API 570, the owner's authorized inspector is the inspector of record, and Atlantis supplies the crack indications and sketches.

Maryland administers a Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Program through its Division of Labor and Industry. Equipment installed in the state must be built to the ASME Code and registered with the National Board, and inspections are performed by commissioned inspectors working for an authorized inspection agency. When a jurisdictional vessel is repaired, the owner's agency decides how repair welds are to be examined. Our explanation of Article 7 goes through the technical requirements, and the complete guide to magnetic particle testing gives wider background.

Technique: yokes, prods, coils and particles

Field work is mostly done with a portable electromagnetic yoke. An AC yoke must lift at least 10 pounds at the pole spacing used and a DC or permanent-magnet yoke at least 40 pounds, and the technician proves it with a test weight. Where a yoke cannot reach enough field in a thick section, prods or a coil are used under a procedure that fixes current to thickness.

Dry powder works well on rough, outdoor welds. Wet suspension applied from an aerosol or bath is more sensitive, and fluorescent versions give the highest sensitivity but need UV-A light and a darkened area, with the intensity and ambient-light limits fixed in the Article. A field indicator confirms strength and direction. Every area is examined twice with fields at roughly right angles. After examination, the part is demagnetized when residual magnetism would affect later welding, machining, instruments or bearings.

Salt air, humidity and surface condition

Waterfront steel arrives in poor condition, and surface condition drives the quality of the result. Rust, marine growth, grease, paint and weld spatter all interfere. The owner arranges blasting, wire brushing or grinding to bare metal at the weld and a margin on each side, and the technician cleans the final surface. Thin firmly bonded coatings can be examined through if the procedure has been demonstrated to work through them at that thickness.

Humidity and fog produce condensation that dilutes wet particle suspensions and breaks the particle film. Dew on morning steel is common near the harbor, so the technician may dry the surface, warm it or use dry powder. Winter cold stiffens suspensions and ice kills contrast. The procedure sets the permitted temperature range, and the report records the conditions.

Who performs the examination

Level II technicians perform and interpret the examination under Atlantis's written practice, which follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and an ASNT Level III approves the procedure and reviews reports. Atlantis has no office in Baltimore, so technicians are mobilized to your site for the scope you define. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, and the technician brings calibrated equipment and the approved procedure.

Crane structures, repair pads and lifting gear

Cranes and lifting appliances are examined where load paths change direction: boom hinge pins and lugs, sheave brackets, trolley wheel assemblies, spreader beam welds and the corners of cutouts. Ship repair work adds temporary attachments such as pad eyes, brackets and strongbacks, which are cut off after use, and the area where they were welded is ground and examined so that no crack is left in the parent plate. A removed lug is a classic place for a surface crack to hide under a fresh grind mark.

Lifting gear is examined to the owner's inspection program or the lifting standard that applies, and acceptance is often stricter than a general fabrication code. Hooks, shackles and links are examined for cracks at the shank, the saddle and the thread. Tell us which standard governs, and whether the owner allows paint removal on load-bearing parts, because the technician cannot examine a surface that is not bare.

Reading indications and avoiding false calls

Particles also collect at the edge of a weld cap, at sharp changes of section and where another magnet has touched the part. The technician sorts those non-relevant indications from real ones by demagnetizing, cleaning and reexamining in a different direction, or by lightly dressing the surface. Real indications are measured, and their length and shape decide which rule in the acceptance table applies. Cracks and lack of fusion are rejected at any size. Rejectable areas are marked on the steel and photographed if the owner wants a record, and the site contact hears about them before the technician leaves.

What the magnetic particle report contains

The report names the component and drawing, the procedure revision and code edition, the yoke or other equipment with its lifting-power check, the particles and lighting, the surface condition, and the technician and Level III reviewer. Each indication is listed with location, orientation and length and is accepted or rejected against the named criteria. Sketches or photographs are attached, and any area that could not be examined is listed with the reason. The field-strength check on the part is recorded as well, so a reader months later can see that the setup was verified instead of assumed.

A marked-up photograph taken before grinding is often the only evidence that survives once a repair is made. It lets the owner's engineer judge whether similar welds elsewhere on the same crane, pier fitting or vessel deserve a closer look, and it gives the repair crew the exact location and orientation of each crack.

Weld repairs and the examination sequence

On repairs, magnetic particle testing is used at three points: after the defect is ground out to prove the crack is gone, after the repair weld, and, for thick or restrained steel, after a delay that allows hydrogen cracking to appear. Many welding procedures require that delay before the final examination, and it can add a day to the schedule that the owner should plan for. Ask your welding engineer which holds apply, and tell us so that the technician returns at the right time.

Planning a magnetic particle job in Baltimore

Give us the season, the surface condition and whether the work is indoors or exposed. Many harbor sites are secure facilities that need a Transportation Worker Identification Credential, safety orientation and an escort, and elevated welds on cranes and piers need lift or scaffold access that the owner supplies. Arrange lighting for fluorescent work and shade for daylight work. Tell us how the job connects to I-95, I-695 and the tunnels so travel is planned, and expect dates to be confirmed when the scope is agreed.

Limited access and awkward geometry

Waterfront steel is rarely convenient. Welds sit under pier decks, inside crane legs, behind machinery guards and at the bottom of tanks and voids. A yoke is compact, which helps, but the technician still needs room to place the poles, apply particles and see the result, so tell us about confined spaces, working at height and any lighting limits. Where access is poor, the owner may need to arrange scaffold, a lift or a small cut-out, and the report will state any weld length that could not be reached.

Choosing between magnetic particle, penetrant and ultrasonic testing

Use magnetic particle testing for surface cracks in carbon steel. Use penetrant testing on stainless, aluminum and other non-magnetic metal, and ultrasonic testing when weld volume or remaining wall matters. The MT versus PT comparison helps with the choice, and the national magnetic particle testing page describes the service.

Training your own magnetic particle technicians

Atlantis teaches MT Level 1 training and MT Level 2 training. Hands-on practice and the practical exam are arranged by your company under its own written practice. See the Baltimore NDT training page or the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker.

faq.q: What steel can be examined by magnetic particle testing in Baltimore?
faq.a: Carbon steel and most low-alloy steel, which covers most crane, pier, ship repair and structural work. Stainless steel, aluminum and copper alloys are not magnetic, so those parts need liquid penetrant testing instead.

faq.q: Can magnetic particle testing find cracks hidden inside a weld?
faq.a: No. It finds surface cracks and flaws just under the surface. For the interior of a weld or remaining wall thickness, ultrasonic testing is used, and many Baltimore jobs combine both methods on the same weld.

faq.q: Why is each area examined in two directions?
faq.a: A crack parallel to the magnetic field gives little flux leakage and can be missed. ASME Section V Article 7 calls for two examinations with the field at roughly right angles so cracks in any direction show.

faq.q: Can marine paint stay on the steel during the examination?
faq.a: Thin, firmly bonded coating may stay if the procedure has been demonstrated through it at that thickness. Thick or flaking paint, rust and marine growth must be removed so particles can reach the surface.

faq.q: How do humid or foggy conditions affect the work?
faq.a: Condensation dilutes wet suspensions and breaks the particle film. The technician dries or warms the steel, or switches to dry powder, and records the conditions in the report so the examination can be judged later.

faq.q: Is demagnetization always required?
faq.a: No. It is required when residual magnetism could affect later welding, machining, instruments or bearing surfaces. The procedure says when, and the report states whether it was done and checked afterward.

faq.q: Who decides if an indication is acceptable?
faq.a: The technician judges it against the acceptance criteria in the governing code. On in-service equipment the owner's authorized inspector or engineer then makes the repair or keep-running call from the data.

faq.q: Do I need a Transportation Worker Identification Credential for the job?
faq.a: Many secure areas of marine terminals require one, along with safety orientation and an escort. Tell us early which areas are involved so access can be arranged before the technician travels to the site.

faq.q: Can my staff learn magnetic particle testing instead of outsourcing?
faq.a: Yes. MT Level 1 and Level 2 courses are available. Your company supplies the hands-on practice and the practical exam, and certifies its own people under SNT-TC-1A.

pt.title: Liquid Penetrant Testing & Dye Penetrant | Baltimore, MD
pt.description: Dye penetrant inspection for stainless, aluminum and nickel alloy welds, piping and castings in Baltimore, MD. ASNT Level II technicians. Get a quote.
pt.h1: Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT) in Baltimore, Maryland
pt.html:
Liquid penetrant testing finds cracks, pores and laps that break the surface of any non-porous material, which makes it the method for stainless steel, aluminum, bronze and nickel alloys. Atlantis NDT mobilizes Level II technicians to Baltimore for dye penetrant inspection of welds, castings, machined parts and repairs at ship repair yards, plants and shops. Describe the material and finish in a quote request and we reply within one business day.

Where penetrant testing is used in Baltimore

Salt water makes alloys common on the waterfront. Ships and workboats carry bronze propellers and fittings, stainless piping and aluminum structure, and repair yards examine those parts when they are welded, machined or reworked. Marine terminals and power plants use stainless and alloy piping, valve bodies and heat exchangers that are examined after repair. Cargo-handling and offshore-style equipment brings aluminum and stainless components that cannot be magnetized.

The same applies inland. Food and sugar processors, chemical blenders, pharmaceutical suppliers and hospital plants all operate stainless vessels and sanitary piping, where welds must be inspected without being contaminated. Machine shops and foundries in the region produce castings and machined parts that are checked for surface porosity and cracks. Redevelopment at Sparrows Point and ship repair around the harbor generate repair welds on mixed materials, and each of those welds is a place where penetrant testing is routinely specified.

What the method finds and what it misses

A thin liquid enters surface-breaking discontinuities by capillary action. After the surface is wiped and a developer is applied, the trapped liquid bleeds back and marks the crack. It finds cracks, seams, laps, cold shuts and open porosity in metals, ceramics and some plastics.

Its limits are the flip side of that mechanism. A discontinuity that does not reach the surface is invisible, so internal weld flaws and wall loss need ultrasonic testing. Smeared metal from grinding, blasting or machining can close a crack so that nothing enters, and oil, paint, salt and corrosion products can block it too. Rough or porous surfaces hold penetrant and give a noisy background. Cleaning therefore decides whether the examination is meaningful. On carbon steel, magnetic particle inspection in Baltimore is often faster, and for the interior of a weld use ultrasonic testing in Baltimore.

Codes and acceptance criteria

Procedures follow ASME Section V Article 6 and ASTM E165, with ASTM E1417 where a specification calls for it. Acceptance comes from the governing code: ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 8 for vessels, ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.4 and Table 341.3.2 for process piping, ASME B31.1 for power piping, and AWS D1.1 where penetrant testing is specified on structural welds. Under API 510, API 570 and API 653 the owner's authorized inspector is the inspector of record and Atlantis reports the examination data.

Maryland's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Program, run by the Division of Labor and Industry, requires installed equipment to be built to the ASME Code and registered with the National Board, with inspections by commissioned inspectors from an authorized inspection agency. When a jurisdictional vessel is repaired, penetrant testing is often how stainless and alloy repair welds are examined, and the agency decides what is required. Our article on Section V Article 6 sets out the rules in detail.

Penetrant systems and material control

Penetrants are either visible or fluorescent, and are removed by solvent, water or an emulsifier. Visible solvent-removable penetrant in aerosol cans is the common field kit for weld work on a pier, in a plant or in a yard, since it needs no darkened area. Fluorescent penetrant is more sensitive and is examined under UV-A light in a dark space, which suits shop work and critical components. Water-washable systems fit production parts and castings.

Chemistry matters near salt water and on alloys. Materials used on austenitic stainless steel, nickel alloys and titanium must be controlled for sulfur, chlorine and fluorine content so that they do not damage the metal in service. The technician uses controlled products and records the brand and batch in the report.

How a penetrant examination is carried out

The technician cleans the surface, lets it dry, applies penetrant and holds it for the dwell time that the procedure sets. Excess is removed, developer is applied as a thin even film, and the area is read after the development time and watched as indications grow. Visible work needs a light level that is measured, and fluorescent work needs UV-A intensity and low ambient light that are measured.

Temperature is a hard limit. Article 6 of ASME Section V gives a standard window of 40 to 125 degrees Fahrenheit for both part and materials, and anything outside it means qualifying the procedure at the real temperature. Cold, damp harbor mornings and sun-heated steel in summer both fall outside the range, so surface temperature is measured and recorded.

Bronze, castings and machined parts

Castings are examined for surface porosity, shrinkage cracks and cold shuts, and bronze propellers and fittings need a careful look at blade roots and edges where fatigue and cavitation damage start. A machined surface can smear metal over a crack, so examination after rough machining and again at finished size is common. Raw castings have rough skin that holds penetrant, so a water-washable system or extra cleaning may be needed. Tell the technician whether the part is raw, rough machined or finished, and send the drawing, because the accept or reject decision depends on the area and the stress it sees.

Sanitary stainless in food, pharmaceutical and hospital plants

Stainless vessels and piping in processing plants must be left clean after examination, and the quality department usually specifies the cleaning and rinse. Agree the solvent, the removal method, the developer and the final rinse before the visit, and agree how waste is handled on the site. The technician controls chlorine and sulfur content in the products, protects gaskets and elastomers from solvent, and keeps developer away from product-contact surfaces where it cannot be removed.

Reading indications and repair sequence

Relevant indications come from real discontinuities. Non-relevant ones come from rough weld ripple, machining marks, crevices and leftover penetrant, and the technician can wipe the spot, reapply developer and look again to settle a doubtful call. On repairs, the cavity is examined after the defect is ground out to prove the crack is gone, the repair is welded, and the finished weld is examined again. Agree that sequence with your welding engineer before work starts, and place the final examination after any heat treatment or pressure test that could open a tight crack.

Cleaning before and after

The quality of cleaning decides whether the examination means anything. Solvents, detergents and mechanical cleaning remove oil, grease, paint and scale, and the part must dry fully, because solvent trapped in a crack dilutes the penetrant and weakens the indication. After examination, developer and penetrant residue are removed, which matters for parts that will be welded, for equipment in cleanliness-controlled service and for stainless surfaces that contact product. Agree who supplies cleaning materials and how rags and cans are disposed of before work begins.

Who performs the work

Level II technicians perform and interpret penetrant examinations under Atlantis's written practice, which follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and an ASNT Level III approves procedures and reviews reports. Technicians come to your site from outside the city, because Atlantis has no office in Baltimore. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001.

What the penetrant report contains

The report names the component, material, drawing and weld numbers, the procedure revision and code edition, and the penetrant, remover and developer brand and batch. It records surface temperature, dwell and development times, the technician and Level III reviewer, and each indication with its type, location and size. Every indication is accepted or rejected against the named criteria, photographs or sketches are attached where useful, and any area that could not be examined is listed with the reason.

Planning a penetrant job in Baltimore

Salt and chlorides are the main enemy of a clean surface. Marine salt dries in cracks and on the metal and must be washed out before the penetrant goes on, and the owner has to arrange washing, blasting or brushing as the surface requires. Fog and dew slow drying, so allow time and shelter. Tell us whether the parts are raw, ground or finished, because etching may be needed to reopen cracks after grinding, and the owner has to approve etching on finished parts.

Many harbor facilities are secure areas that call for a Transportation Worker Identification Credential, orientation and an escort. Give us the site location relative to I-95, I-695 and the tunnels so travel can be planned, and expect dates to be confirmed when the scope is agreed. Plan waste handling for solvent, rags and developer residue under the site's rules.

Exposed harbor work often needs a tent or windbreak, because wind carries spray and dust onto freshly developed surfaces and rain washes the developer away. Where the owner cannot provide cover, schedule around the weather window and tell the technician which surfaces will be exposed. After the work, the area is wiped clean so that no film is left on steel that will be painted or welded next.

Documentation for customers and surveyors

Penetrant records often travel beyond the plant. A shipowner, a surveyor, a food-safety auditor or an insurer may ask to see how a repair weld was proved clean, so the report is written to stand on its own. It lists the materials by batch, the surface temperature, the times and the indications, and it states what was not examined. If your customer requires a particular format or an inspection plan reference, send it with the quote request.

Choosing between penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing

Use penetrant testing for stainless steel, aluminum, bronze, nickel alloys and parts that cannot be magnetized. Use magnetic particle testing on carbon steel when speed matters, and ultrasonic testing for the weld interior or remaining wall. The MT versus PT comparison helps decide between the surface methods, and the national penetrant testing page describes the service.

Training your own penetrant technicians

Atlantis teaches PT Level 1 training and PT Level 2 training, and learners can practice on the penetrant testing simulator. The employer arranges hands-on work and the practical exam and certifies its own people. See the Baltimore NDT training page.

faq.q: Which materials can liquid penetrant testing inspect in Baltimore?
faq.a: Any non-porous material: stainless steel, aluminum, bronze, titanium, nickel alloys and carbon steel, plus ceramics and some plastics. It suits the alloy fittings, castings and piping common in marine and process work.

faq.q: Can penetrant testing find flaws inside a weld?
faq.a: No. It reveals only discontinuities open to the surface. Internal weld quality and wall loss need ultrasonic testing, and many jobs use both methods together on the same weld.

faq.q: What temperature limits apply to penetrant testing?
faq.a: The standard window in Section V Article 6 runs from 40 to 125 degrees Fahrenheit. Beyond it, the procedure needs qualification at the actual temperature, so damp winter mornings and sun-heated summer steel call for planning.

faq.q: Why does salt contamination matter?
faq.a: Dried marine salt and corrosion products can seal crack openings and leave residue that keeps penetrant out. The surface must be washed, brushed or blasted and dried fully before the penetrant is applied.

faq.q: Does penetrant testing damage stainless steel or nickel alloys?
faq.a: Not when the materials are controlled. The procedure limits sulfur, chlorine and fluorine content for those metals, the technician uses suitable products, and the report records the brand and batch used.

faq.q: Is visible or fluorescent penetrant used in the field?
faq.a: Visible solvent-removable penetrant is the usual field choice because it needs no darkened area. Fluorescent penetrant is more sensitive and is used where UV-A light and a dark space can be arranged.

faq.q: What is the right order for inspecting a weld repair?
faq.a: Examine the cavity after grinding to prove the defect is out, weld the repair, then examine the finished weld. Place the final examination after any heat treatment or pressure test required for the item.

faq.q: Who decides whether an indication is rejectable?
faq.a: The technician evaluates each indication against the code acceptance criteria and records the result. For in-service equipment, the owner's authorized inspector or engineer makes the repair or continued-service decision.

faq.q: Can my staff learn penetrant testing instead of using a contractor?
faq.a: Yes. PT Level 1 and Level 2 courses are available with simulator practice. Your company supplies hands-on work and the practical exam, and certifies its own technicians under its written practice.

rt.title: Radiographic Testing (RT) Alternatives | Baltimore, MD
rt.description: Radiography is not offered by Atlantis in the United States. For Baltimore, MD we provide UT as a volumetric alternative and Level III review of RT work.
rt.h1: Radiographic Testing (RT) in Baltimore, Maryland: What Atlantis Offers
rt.html:
Radiography is not something Atlantis does in the United States. To be exact, Atlantis does not offer radiographic testing in Baltimore or anywhere else in the country, because industrial radiography is a licensed activity under Nuclear Regulatory Commission rules, 10 CFR Part 34, or the equivalent rules of an Agreement State. If you came here searching for radiographic testing in Baltimore, this page sets out the related work we can do.

Ultrasonic examination as the volumetric option

Many Baltimore welds on piping, vessels and structural steel can be examined by ultrasonic methods when the code allows it. ASME B31.3 and API 1104 contain provisions for ultrasonic examination of production welds, AWS D1.1 has ultrasonic acceptance criteria for groove welds, and ASME Section VIII permits ultrasonic examination in place of radiography only under specific conditions. Substitution is never assumed. The owner, the engineer and, on code work, the authorized inspector have to agree on it before the job begins.

Technicians travel to the site for the agreed scope, and Atlantis has no office in Baltimore. Read about ultrasonic testing in Baltimore for the technique, the national ultrasonic testing page for the service, and the ultrasonic testing guide for background.

ASNT Level III review that needs no radiation licence

Owners in the Baltimore area often receive film or digital images from a licensed contractor and want an independent opinion. An ASNT Level III can review the images and technique sheets against ASME Section V Article 2 and the construction code, give a second read on a disputed indication, check that image quality indicators and technique match the requirement, and review a contractor's procedure and written practice. Because it is a review of records and images, no radiation licence is involved. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, leads this review. Atlantis does not name or recommend radiography contractors, and choosing one stays with the owner.

Programs can also be strengthened through our Level III consulting service and written practice development.

Radiographic theory courses

Personnel who need to understand radiographic technique can study theory in the radiographic testing Level 2 course, which covers principles, exposure geometry, image quality and code interpretation. Practical exposure work, including source handling and radiation safety, needs a licensed employer with an established radiation safety program, so that part is the employer's responsibility, and the employer certifies its own personnel under its written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. See the Baltimore NDT training page for the wider training route.

What to send with an enquiry

A short package speeds the conversation. Send the drawing or isometric, the weld numbers, the governing code and edition, the material and thickness, and the contract clause that calls for volumetric examination. Say whether the owner has already agreed to ultrasonic examination in place of film or image work, and name the authorized inspector or engineer who will accept the results. With that information the scope, the procedure and the Level III review can be defined quickly and without guesswork.

Other conventional methods in Baltimore

Surface examinations can be done during the same visit. Magnetic particle inspection in Baltimore covers carbon steel welds and liquid penetrant testing in Baltimore covers stainless steel, aluminum, bronze and nickel alloys. To discuss a Baltimore scope, send a quote request and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is radiography on a Baltimore job something Atlantis handles?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not offer radiographic testing in the United States because industrial radiography is licensed under NRC rules or Agreement State rules. We offer ultrasonic examination and Level III review instead.

faq.q: Is ultrasonic testing accepted in place of radiography?
faq.a: Only where the code permits it and the owner, engineer and authorized inspector agree beforehand. ASME B31.3, API 1104, AWS D1.1 and ASME Section VIII each treat ultrasonic examination differently, so check the specific rule.

faq.q: What does a Level III review of radiographic images cover?
faq.a: It covers images and technique sheets checked against ASME Section V Article 2 and the construction code, a second read of disputed indications, and review of a contractor's procedure and written practice, all without a radiation licence.

faq.q: Will Atlantis recommend a radiography company in Baltimore?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not name or recommend radiography contractors. Once you have chosen one, we can review its procedure, written practice and images and give you an independent technical opinion.

faq.q: Can technicians study radiography theory with Atlantis?
faq.a: Yes, through a radiographic testing Level 2 theory course. Hands-on exposure work must be arranged by a licensed employer, and the employer certifies its own personnel under its written practice.
